facts.fact_text: Some of the applications raise an issue concerning the right to freedom of peaceful assembly in connection with the applicants' protests against the landfill site near the town of Klin, Moscow Region.
The applicants live in the town of Klin, Moscow Region.
The villages of Novotschapovo, Bol'shoye Tschapovo, Golikovo and Opritovo are located near each other in the Klin District.
The villages of Novotschapovo, Bol'shoye Tschapovo, Golikovo and Opritovo are located between 5.8 and 13 km from Aleksinskiy Quarry.
Since 1993 Aleksinskiy Quarry has been used as a landfill site for solid household waste collected in the Klin District.
Aleksinskiy Quarry is currently operated by the waste management company Kombinat LLC (OOO Комбинат).
Kombinat LLC (OOO Комбинат) operates Aleksinskiy Quarry pursuant to a lease agreement dated 12 November 2009 with the Klin municipal administration.
The applicants alleged that large amounts of solid waste had been taken to Aleksinskiy Quarry daily and deposited in the landfill site, in violation of the applicable environmental regulations.
The applicants alleged that the unlawful operation of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had caused a strong foul odour in Klin and the areas nearby.
The applicants alleged that the unlawful operation of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had caused air pollution in Klin and the areas nearby.
The applicants alleged that the unlawful operation of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had caused groundwater contamination in Klin and the areas nearby.
The applicants alleged that the unlawful operation of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had caused the circulation of waste particles in the air in Klin and the areas nearby.
The applicants alleged that the large numbers of scavenging birds at the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had threatened air safety in the area.
A military airbase known as Klin-5 was situated within 3 km of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The military airbase Klin-5 was situated in proximity to the applicants' houses.

A large-scale multi-level solid waste recycling and processing plant (комбинат по переработке отходов (КПО) «Алексинский карьер» – the waste processing plant) was set up at the site of Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry started operations at the end of 2019.
The project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been discussed at a public hearing.

The project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had received a positive conclusion from the authorities concerning the assessment of its impact on the environment.
The first applicant explained at the hearing that he owned and had been cultivating a plot of land in the village of Bol'shoye Tschapovo in the Klin District of Moscow Region.

The first applicant explained at the hearing that since 2015, every day, especially on hot days or in the evening, there had been a strong foul odour which had made him feel frustrated, physically and mentally unwell, had caused him to have mood swings and had made him lose the desire to work and unable to sleep.
The first applicant explained at the hearing that since 2015 he had experienced headaches and nausea so badly that he could not even eat.
The first applicant explained at the hearing that the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been the source of the foul waste odour, which had been confirmed by multiple complaints from local residents.

The first applicant explained at the hearing that the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been the source of the foul waste odour, which had been confirmed by the head of the regional administrative and technical supervisory body in a press release of 20 July 2016.

Witnesses A., Ch., Ey. and An., who lived in the villages close to Aleksinskiy Quarry, testified at the hearing that since 2015 there had regularly been a strong unpleasant odour emanating from the quarry.

The Klin Town Court of Moscow Region held that Kombinat LLC had been sanctioned in administrative proceedings on 7 April 2015 for failure to register as a waste management company in the State landfill register.
The Klin Town Court of Moscow Region held that Kombinat LLC had been sanctioned in administrative proceedings on 15 July 2015 for failing to obtain a licence to emit harmful substances.
On 7 April 2015 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for failing to register in the State landfill register.
On 15 July 2015 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for failing to register in the State landfill register.

On 15 July 2015 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for operating without a licence to emit certain harmful substances into the atmospheric air and without established emission limits, imposing a fine (amount left blank in the published copy of the judgment).

On 3 March 2017 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for illegally depositing waste beyond the designated boundaries of Aleksinskiy Quarry, imposing a fine of RUB 150,000 (about EUR 1,700).
On 4 August 2017 the Consumer Protection Authority sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings (details set out in paragraphs 18-22 and 25 of the judgment).
On 13 October 2017 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings (details set out in paragraphs 19-20 of the judgment).

On 15 December 2017 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for emitting toxic elements above the maximum permitted levels (MPL) registered on 6 September 2017, specifically ammonia at 3 MPL, nitrogen oxide at 53 MPL, phenol at 93.8 MPL, soot at 1.3 MPL, and xylol at 2.3 MPL, imposing a fine of RUB 90,000 (about EUR 1,000).
On 19 December 2017 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings (details set out in paragraph 22 of the judgment).

On 24 April 2018 the Commercial Court of Moscow Region sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for failing to construct a protective barrier around Aleksinskiy Quarry to prevent the spread of fragments of waste, thus endangering people's lives and health and creating various environmental hazards, imposing a fine of RUB 100,000 (about EUR 1,000).

On 7 May 2018 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for emitting toxic elements above the maximum permitted levels (MPL) registered on 8 February 2018, specifically nitrogen dioxide at 2.2-12.8 MPL, imposing a fine of RUB 100,000.

On 7 May 2018 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for failing to mention in its report on emissions a degasification furnace that releases carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxide, imposing a fine (amount left blank in the published copy of the judgment).

On 7 May 2018 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for failing to keep land adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry free of uncollected fragments of waste and for depositing unauthorised types of waste, imposing a fine of RUB 140,000 (about EUR 1,600).

On 15 May 2018 the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment sanctioned Kombinat LLC for emitting ammonia 3.9-17 times above the maximum permitted level (MPL), as detected during an inspection on 27 April 2018 at air monitoring posts in the villages near Aleksinskiy Quarry, and ordered Kombinat LLC to ensure compliance with its emissions permit by 26 January 2019.

On 17 May 2018 a State body issued an order to Kombinat LLC to comply with the relevant environmental regulations after finding that Kombinat LLC had deposited 833,186.20 tonnes of waste in 2017, above the authorised limit of 270,000 tonnes of waste per year.
On 19 June 2018 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for depositing unauthorised waste of type II hazard, imposing a fine of RUB 120,000 (about EUR 1,400).

On 13 December 2018 the Klin Town Court sanctioned Kombinat LLC in administrative proceedings for operating without a positive assessment of the environmental impact of its activities and in the absence of an established sanitary protection zone.

At the hearing of 7 April 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 1), the representative of Kombinat LLC explained that the company had been taking steps to have itself listed in the State landfill register.

At the hearing of 7 April 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 1), the representative of Kombinat LLC explained that the authorities had not yet taken a decision on registering Kombinat LLC in the State landfill register.
At the hearing of 15 July 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 3), the representative of Kombinat LLC stated that no measurements of emissions from Aleksinskiy Quarry had been carried out.

At the hearing of 15 July 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 3), the representative of Kombinat LLC stated that Aleksinskiy Quarry was the only place for household waste disposal in the Klin District.

At the hearing of 15 July 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 3), the representative of Kombinat LLC stated that the suspension of Kombinat LLC's operations would be very damaging to the local environment.

At the hearing of 15 July 2015 (administrative proceedings no. 3), the representative of Kombinat LLC explained that the authorities had not yet registered Kombinat LLC in the State landfill register.

On 4 August 2017 the Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA), acting upon complaints by an unidentified number of people allegedly affected by the activities of Kombinat LLC, carried out an inspection at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA) concluded that in the course of its waste processing operations Kombinat LLC had breached sixteen environmental, sanitary and epidemiological regulations.
The Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA) ordered Kombinat LLC to suspend its operations and carry out remedial measures by 1 May 2018.
On 11 August 2017 the Klin Town Court terminated the administrative proceedings against Kombinat LLC, finding the results of the inspection of 4 August 2017 unsubstantiated.

An inspector of the Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA) appealed against the Klin Town Court's decision of 11 August 2017 terminating the administrative proceedings against Kombinat LLC.
On 7 September 2017 the Moscow Regional Court remitted the case against Kombinat LLC to the Klin Town Court for fresh examination.

On 13 October 2017 the Klin Town Court confirmed the conclusions of the inspection of 4 August 2017 and found Kombinat LLC liable for breaching sixteen relevant sanitary, epidemiological and environmental regulations.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included Kombinat LLC's failure to obtain the approval of the chief environmental health officer (Главный санитарный врач) for the creation of a sanitary protection zone around Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included insufficient soil supply for the intermediary and final stages of waste separation at Aleksinskiy Quarry, resulting in uncovered and visible waste remains.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included leftover waste (mainly plastic rubbish bags) on the boundary of Aleksinskiy Quarry adjacent to the villages of Naprugovo and Novotschapovo.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included the absence of gas control systems at Aleksinskiy Quarry, which causes an increase in air pollution and has an adverse impact on nearby residential areas.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included the absence of a system for collecting leachates (liquid from rotten waste which endangers the quality of soil, groundwater and surface water) at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included the absence of regular monitoring (once every ten days) of uncollected fragments of waste such as plastic bags and scraps of paper at Aleksinskiy Quarry and failure to take the relevant clean-up measures.

The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included Kombinat LLC's failure to carry out regular cellular morphological and chemical testing of waste components at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The sixteen violations found by the Klin Town Court on 13 October 2017 included Kombinat LLC's failure to make water control facilities at Aleksinskiy Quarry accessible to inspectors' vehicles.
The Klin Town Court ordered Kombinat LLC to immediately suspend its activities for ninety days following the judgment of 13 October 2017.

The Klin Town Court explicitly stated in the operative part of its decision of 13 October 2017 that the lodging of an appeal complaint would not prevent execution of the administrative sanction imposed on Kombinat LLC.

On 13 October 2017 the Klin Town Court granted a request by Kombinat LLC to suspend execution of the administrative sanction of ninety days' suspension of activities, pending the examination of Kombinat LLC's statement of appeal by the Moscow Regional Court.
On 19 December 2017 the Klin Town Court re-examined the case against Kombinat LLC, which had been remitted to it by the Moscow Regional Court.
On 19 December 2017 the Klin Town Court confirmed its earlier conclusions of 13 October 2017 regarding Kombinat LLC's violations.
On 19 December 2017 the Klin Town Court imposed an administrative fine of RUB 250,000 (about EUR 3,000) on Kombinat LLC, which was paid in full.
One of the applicants, Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19), brought a complaint against the Klin Town Court's decision to suspend execution of the administrative sanction against Kombinat LLC.
On 8 February 2018 the Moscow Regional Court allowed Ms Kotova's complaint and quashed the Klin Town Court's decision to suspend execution of the administrative sanction against Kombinat LLC.

No further information was provided to the Court in respect of the proceedings brought by Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) against the decision to suspend execution of the administrative sanction against Kombinat LLC.
On 15 May 2018 another notice of violation was issued to Kombinat LLC stating that the main source of air pollution at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been the body of the landfill itself.

The notice of violation issued to Kombinat LLC on 15 May 2018 stated that hydrogen sulphide, ammonia, methane, benzol, nitrogen dioxide, formaldehyde and other toxic substances had been released into the atmospheric air as a result of waste disposal at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
On 7 June 2018 the Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA) carried out an unannounced inspection at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Consumer Protection Authority of Moscow Region (the regional CPA) established on 7 June 2018 that all the violations detected on 4 August 2017 had been corrected by Kombinat LLC, except the failure to obtain the approval of the chief environmental health officer for a sanitary protection zone around Aleksinskiy Quarry.
On 8 November 2019 the Klin Town Court examined a complaint brought by a group of residents of Klin, including the applicants (except the first, fourth and seventh applicants), against Kombinat LLC.

The group of residents of Klin, including the applicants (except the first, fourth and seventh applicants), requested the Klin Town Court to stop Kombinat LLC's activities and close Aleksinskiy Quarry permanently.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had obtained a State-issued licence to collect and process solid waste, issued in 2007.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had obtained a licence to emit harmful substances within the applicable limits, issued in 2015.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had obtained two positive assessments of the environmental impact of its activities, issued in 2014 and 2015 respectively.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had obtained a positive assessment of its project for a sanitary protection zone, issued in 2016.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had obtained a certificate confirming registration of Aleksinskiy Quarry in the polluting entities register, issued in 2017.

The Klin Town Court examined a report by Mr P., a court-appointed environmental expert, who testified that Kombinat LLC had committed irreversible environmental violations and that waste disposal at Aleksinskiy Quarry should be discontinued immediately.
At the hearing before the Klin Town Court, Mr P. confirmed the conclusions reached in his expert report.
At the hearing before the Klin Town Court, Mr P. explained that he had not tested air quality at Aleksinskiy Quarry, and that the relevant officials should do such tests regularly over a year.
According to Mr P., it was not possible to establish a direct link between the environmental impact of Aleksinskiy Quarry and morbidity rates.
According to Mr P., no technology existed to collect leachate that had already contaminated soil at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
In 1993 a protective plastic liner had been laid at Aleksinskiy Quarry against leachate contamination, but no data was available about its maintenance.
The Klin Town Court found the expert's report by Mr P. unconvincing because Mr P. had not reviewed the relevant project documentation for Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The Klin Town Court found the expert's report by Mr P. unconvincing because Mr P. had not tested air, water and soil quality at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The Klin Town Court found the expert's report by Mr P. unconvincing because Mr P. had not noted any measurements of harmful substances for Aleksinskiy Quarry or Klin.
The Klin Town Court found the expert's report by Mr P. unconvincing because Mr P. had not measured the quantity of waste that had been deposited at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Klin Town Court held that Kombinat LLC had provided reports on air, water and soil quality testing at Aleksinskiy Quarry and beyond its boundaries, carried out between March 2018 and June 2019 by a private laboratory (Promenergo LLC).

According to the reports by Promenergo LLC covering March 2018 to June 2019, the maximum permitted levels (MPL) for nitrogen dioxide, ammonia, carbon monoxide, phenol, formaldehyde, hydrogen sulphide, benzol, methane, xylol and toluene had not been exceeded at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

Excerpts from the reports by Promenergo LLC (at least eight of which from 2018 were provided to the Court) indicate, prima facie, that the maximum permitted levels (MPL) of some substances had been exceeded at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The Klin Town Court found that in June 2019 the director of Kombinat LLC had approved a programme for regular air, water and soil quality testing at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
Reports on air, water and soil quality tests conducted in September 2019 pursuant to Kombinat LLC's programme were submitted to the Klin Town Court.

On 22 August 2019 the Consumer Protection Authority (CPA) approved the project documentation for the creation of a sanitary protection zone around Aleksinskiy Quarry as being compliant with the relevant environmental standards, including those for air quality.
On 23 September 2019 the project documentation for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry was approved by the State authorities.

The commander-in-chief of the military base located in the Klin District informed Kombinat LLC that the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been approved as safe for flights.

The Klin Town Court concluded that the applicants had not submitted solid and convincing proof of a risk of Kombinat LLC causing harm in the future as a result of its activities at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Klin Town Court concluded that the applicants had not submitted solid and convincing proof that the risk of Kombinat LLC causing harm in the future could in fact materialise and that its operations should be shut down.
The Klin Town Court did not take the reports on air quality testing submitted by the applicants into account on the grounds that they had been prepared by the applicants themselves.
The Klin Town Court found that Kombinat LLC had submitted proof of compliance of its operations with the applicable standards and regulations.

The Klin Town Court held that the fact that courts and administrative bodies had sanctioned Kombinat LLC eight times in the past for different violations of sanitary and environmental regulations could not justify shutting down its operations because it had not been proven that those violations had caused irreversible damage to the environment.
On 2 March 2020 the Moscow Regional Court dismissed an appeal by the applicants against the Klin Town Court's judgment of 8 November 2019.
The applicants did not provide the Court with a copy of the Moscow Regional Court's judgment of 2 March 2020.

The applicants submitted that they had tried to bring further cassation appeals before the higher courts, but that their appeals had been returned to them for what they described as 'contrived' procedural reasons.
It appears from the relevant domestic decisions submitted by the applicants that they did not comply with the procedural requirements for filing cassation appeals.

On 28 July 2021 the Klin Town Court refused a request by the applicants to re-examine the case anew because they had sought the reassessment of evidence that had already been examined at the hearing of 8 November 2019, which was not considered a valid reason for reopening the proceedings.
Some of the applicants, together with other residents of Klin, brought administrative proceedings in connection with the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

Some of the applicants alleged that the public hearing and procedure for approval of the project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been tainted with certain defects.
The domestic courts dismissed the applicants' complaints concerning the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The domestic courts established, on the basis of the evidence examined, that all procedural requirements had been observed by the respective authorities in relation to the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry, and that those authorities had acted within their powers.

The domestic courts found that there was nothing to indicate that the applicants' rights had been breached in the process of approving the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
In March 2018 the applicants started organising protests against the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
All the applicants except Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) were charged with various administrative offences in connection with their protests against the landfill site.
The details concerning the charges against the applicants, their arrest and the administrative sanctions imposed on them in connection with their protests are outlined in Appendix I of the judgment.
In November 2017 Mr Kotov submitted three notices of a public event (meeting) to the Klin municipal administration.
In May 2018 Mr Kotov submitted one notice of an environmental protest car rally to the Klin municipal administration.
Neither of Mr Kotov's applications to the Klin municipal administration for a public event or environmental protest car rally was approved.
Mr Kotov brought a complaint against the Klin municipal authorities before the courts in connection with the non-approval of his applications for public events.
The details of the proceedings brought by Mr Kotov against the Klin municipal authorities are outlined in Appendix I (application no. 56764/18) of the judgment.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region highlighted the deteriorating environmental situation in Moscow Region and the need to implement modern waste processing technologies.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region requested the President to order the closure of twenty-four landfills in Moscow Region owing to their excessive storage capacity and obsolete technical characteristics.

In 2017 and 2018 State laboratories of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of Moscow Region and of the State Fire and Rescue Service and Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring carried out air quality tests in the vicinity of Aleksinskiy Quarry and in Klin.
From December 2018 to November 2019 a public interest group carried out measurements of air quality in the vicinity of Aleksinskiy Quarry and in Klin, using special testing equipment.

Excerpts from air testing reports produced by State laboratories indicate a number of instances where the maximum permitted levels (MPL) in the atmospheric air of Klin and its districts had been exceeded.
On other dates, air quality measurements in Klin and its districts indicated no excess of the maximum permitted levels (MPL).

A report of the state laboratory dated 15 March 2018 of air sampling in some of the villages near Aleksinskiy Quarry stated that a foul odour typical for landfills had been smelled in the village of Novotschapovo.
The state laboratory report dated 15 March 2018 stated that residents of the village of Novotschapovo should complain to the relevant authorities about the foul odour.

A notice of violation issued to Kombinat LLC by the Moscow Regional Department of the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment on 17 May 2018 stated that Aleksinskiy Quarry had exceeded its storage capacity by three times, with 833,186.20 tonnes of waste deposited in 2017 instead of an anticipated 270,000 tonnes.

According to a letter dated 16 July 2018 from the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring, the level of pollution in Klin had been classified as 'high', mostly owing to an overconcentration of formaldehyde in the atmospheric air.

The letter dated 16 July 2018 from the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring stated that the high concentration of formaldehyde in June 2018 in Klin could be explained by a certain type of repair works carried out at the time, solar radiation or certain chemical reactions.

According to an expert report dated 22 August 2019 concerning the project for a sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry, 1,662,625 tonnes of waste had been deposited at Aleksinskiy Quarry between mid-2017 and mid-2019.
The applicants submitted that the 1,662,625 tonnes of waste deposited at Aleksinskiy Quarry between mid-2017 and mid-2019 had been almost three times above the authorised limit for waste disposal.

A forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 submitted by Mr P. in reply to questions of the Klin Town Court concluded that the source of the 'foul landfill odour' could only have been the body of the landfill itself at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry was the only place in the vicinity of Klin that attracted large numbers of birds.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the violation by Kombinat LLC of sanitary, epidemiological and environmental regulations had resulted in detectable consequences for the environment and the health of the population.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the massive uncontrolled leakage of toxic organic waste (leachate) from Aleksinskiy Quarry had been practically impossible to remediate and had posed a real danger to the life and health of the population.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the leachate from Aleksinskiy Quarry had seriously endangered the environment, had impaired the quality of fresh water and groundwater, and could contaminate soil and water sources for decades.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that Kombinat LLC had deposited waste beyond the established boundaries of the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry and had exceeded the landfill's authorised capacity for waste disposal.

In the opinion of forensic expert Mr P. in his report dated 31 July 2019, Kombinat LLC should have been ordered to take measures to prevent further breaches and to repair the damage caused at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Government submitted that within the framework of the 2018 Russia-wide 'Ecology' project, plans had been drawn up for the construction of a large-scale multi-level solid waste recycling and processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been planned to carry out the sorting and subsequent recycling of solid waste to help improve the environmental situation in the area.
The processing capacity of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been estimated at between 150,000 and 300,000 tonnes of solid waste per year.

The waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been designed to use the best available national and international technologies aimed at reducing landfill, lowering the risks of gas formation and foul odours and creating recycled fuels.
Kombinat LLC's project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been examined at a public hearing.
Kombinat LLC's project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been submitted for a State environmental impact assessment.

On 23 September 2019 the project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been approved for implementation by the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment.
On 22 August 2019 the project for delimiting a 1.5 km sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been studied by the relevant State expert commission.

On 23 October 2019 the project for delimiting a 1.5 km sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been approved by the Russian Consumer Protection Authority (CPA) as being in compliance with the relevant regulations.
The Government submitted that in 2019 the regional authorities of Moscow Region had approved an investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry for 2019-2027.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry had been in effect since 1 July 2019.

The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated the construction of systems for collecting and processing landfill gas, collecting leachates and purifying filters.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated the construction of a multi-level solid waste sorting and processing facility.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated sealing the body of the landfill and its borders to prevent leakage.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated collecting rainwater and diverting drainage.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for drainage and the treatment of rainwater at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for acoustic protection from birds at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for electronically controlling the amount of waste taken to Aleksinskiy Quarry by trucks to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for collecting, decontaminating and disposing of landfill gas at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC started constructing a reverse osmosis system for treating leachate at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
Kombinat LLC regularly (every three months) monitored emissions into the air, water and soil at Aleksinskiy Quarry and published the results of its inspections on the quarry's website.
Kombinat LLC complied with the judgment of 13 October 2017 of the Klin Town Court by paying the fine imposed on it in full.

Kombinat LLC carried out the relevant remedial measures for violations of the relevant sanitary regulations following the judgment of 13 October 2017 of the Klin Town Court, which had been confirmed by the supervisory State bodies.

The Government submitted that according to reports on atmospheric air, wastewater and groundwater quality testing carried out between 21 March 2018 and 10 June 2019 within and outside the boundaries of Aleksinskiy Quarry, the maximum permitted levels (MPL) of nitrogen dioxide, ammonia, carbon monoxide, phenol, xylol and toluene had not been exceeded.
The Government submitted that in 2018-2019 weekly air quality monitoring had been carried out in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry within 500 metres to 2 km.
Of the 1,206 air samples taken in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry, 1,170 were tested.

The air quality testing in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry indicated that the concentrations of hydrogen sulphide, ammonia, methane, methanethiol, sulphur dioxide and phenol had been within the relevant maximum permitted levels (MPL).
Water quality monitoring in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry had not revealed excessive concentrations of harmful substances.
Testing of groundwater from wells and boreholes and of soil in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry showed no deviation from the relevant health standards.

On 31 January 2018, during an unannounced inspection by the authorities, concentrations of ammonia above the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL) had been detected at the air monitoring posts at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

As a result of the detection of ammonia above the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL) on 31 January 2018, Kombinat LLC had been ordered to take remedial measures in order to comply with the relevant MPL.

According to Kombinat LLC's letter of 31 January 2019 and supporting documents, Kombinat LLC had complied with the order to take remedial measures to bring ammonia levels within the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL).

The Government submitted that in 2018-2019 the authorities of Moscow Region had received seventy-three requests (обращения) concerning the operation of Aleksinskiy Quarry, including requests to have it closed.
The Government submitted that no complaints (жалобы) had been received by the authorities or regional medical organisations about the negative impact of Aleksinskiy Quarry on people's health.

Representatives of the Ministry of Defence had requested the regional government of Moscow Region to have Aleksinskiy Quarry closed because its use had endangered the safety of military planes from Klin-5 airbase during their flights, owing to the circulation of birds above the quarry.

The authorities stated in reply to the Ministry of Defence's request that there were no grounds to close Aleksinskiy Quarry since the modern waste processing plant would be installed by 2021 and the quarry would no longer pose a danger to aircraft.

Between 18 March 2016 and 29 April 2019 the regional and municipal authorities, including representatives of the Committee on the Environment of Moscow Region legislative authority, held eighteen public meetings in the form of hearings, assize legislative sessions and discussions in respect of operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry and its modernisation.

On 29 April 2019 a public hearing was held on the project for the construction of a waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry in order to obtain the views of residents, including those of the applicants, who provided their observations and objections on the issue.
Following the public hearing of 29 April 2019, the project documentation for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry was sent for a State environmental impact assessment.

Information on air and water pollution as well as radiation in the Russian regions had been regularly published on the website of the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring and had been available to the applicants.
Information about the environmental conditions at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been published and updated by Kombinat LLC on its website.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region, during a meeting with residents of Klin and official representatives of Kombinat LLC, stated that the main complaint by residents was the smell emanating from Aleksinskiy Quarry.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region stated that waste disposal operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been carried out in violation of the applicable regulations.
